_description: Mars's tier table — GENERATED by tools/pipeline/build-body-tiers.js --write (plan 27, the Mars item). The scene cross-fades Mars's map by the TT age of its epoch from `tiers` (ages in Myr before J2000). `kind` names what a map IS: the cited present-day map, or illustration — derived from the present-day map and the MOLA topography (the seas below a cited shoreline contour), or generated. The gate tools/verify/surface-tiers.js checks the files against `files`.

mola.title: MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR), 4 pixel/degree topography, megt90n000cb
mola.format: 1440 x 720 big-endian 16-bit metres above the areoid, the first column at 0°E, the first row at 90°N
mola.citation: Smith, D.E. et al., 2001. Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter: Experiment summary after the first year of global mapping of Mars. JGR 106, 23689–23722.
mola.licence: NASA PDS Geosciences Node — public domain (a US Government work)
mola.cached: data/.cache/mola/ (gitignored; fetched and hash-checked by the script)

derived.note: the present-day map with a depth-shaded sea filled below a shoreline contour of the MOLA topography (the polar caps kept; the method is in the script) — a derivative of the CC BY 4.0 map, labelled "illustration"; the shorelines are a CONTESTED reading of the literature below

generated.note: procedural illustration rendered by this script from seeded 3-D value noise on the sphere (seed 20261106) — no third-party rights; labelled "illustration"

literature.carrHead2003: Carr, M.H. & Head, J.W., 2003. Oceans on Mars: An assessment of the observational evidence and possible fate. JGR 108, 5042 — the Arabia (~−2,090 m) and Deuteronilus (~−3,792 m) shoreline levels; the evidence assessed as suggestive, not conclusive.
literature.diAchilleHynek2010: Di Achille, G. & Hynek, B.M., 2010. Ancient ocean on Mars supported by global distribution of deltas and valleys. Nature Geoscience 3, 459–463 — the deltas and valley networks at the Arabia level in the Noachian/early Hesperian.
literature.hartmannNeukum2001: Hartmann, W.K. & Neukum, G., 2001. Cratering chronology and the evolution of Mars. Space Science Reviews 96, 165–194 — the Noachian/Hesperian boundary ~3.7 Ga, the Hesperian/Amazonian ~3.0 Ga, the Noachian from ~4.1 Ga.
literature.tanaka2014: Tanaka, K.L. et al., 2014. Geologic map of Mars. USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292 — the epochs' surfaces.

tiers.label: The Hesperian — a northern sea below the Deuteronilus shoreline (−3,792 m, Carr & Head 2003), a contested reading (derived)
The Noachian — a northern ocean below the Arabia shoreline (−2,090 m, Carr & Head 2003; Di Achille & Hynek 2010), a contested reading (derived)
The pre-Noachian — the early crust before the Noachian's recorded surfaces (generated)
